calls.head: The Mammoth should tilt the ice
calls.body: The Mammoth have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs near the bottom. Expect the Mammoth to spend more of the night in the Maple Leafs’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

calls.body: The Mammoth shoot from anywhere, and the Maple Leafs are near the bottom of the league at stopping it. Sergei Bobrovsky had better be ready from the opening faceoff.

calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Mammoth
calls.body: On depth, Utah is the league’s best, but Toronto is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 35% chance, and it went the way we feared.

UTA.head: We gave Utah a 65% chance, and they delivered.

surprises.head: Utah’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Utah’s power play created 20.5 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.9 (about 8.4 against Toronto) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 125 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Toronto couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Toronto usually gets worse looks than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: a 3.5% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 5.9% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Keller has three assists as the Mammoth beat the Maple Leafs
paras: Dylan Guenther opened the scoring for the Mammoth on the power play with 13 seconds left in the first. Jack Roslovic made it 1-1 for Toronto midway through the second, and Andrew Peeke restored the Mammoth’s lead less than four minutes later. Roslovic struck again midway through the third to tie it 2-2, but that was the last goal the Maple Leafs would get. Nick Schmaltz put the Mammoth ahead for good on the power play with less than seven minutes left. Clayton Keller finished with three assists.

The Mammoth drove the play, outshooting the Maple Leafs 36-29, and the scoreboard caught up. Sebastian Cossa made 27 saves for the Mammoth, and Sergei Bobrovsky, who gave up five goals in Seattle in his last start, kept the Leafs in it, stopping 33 of 36. The Mammoth moved to 10-6-0 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Maple Leafs fell to 8-7-2, sixth in the Atlantic.

items.text: Mikhail Sergachev has a point in eight straight games.
Dylan Guenther extended his point streak against Toronto to six games.

The Maple Leafs were without Kirill Marchenko, Nick Blankenburg, John Tavares and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Ducks and the Islanders were missing more at the time.
The Mammoth have won both meetings this season.
